sources.entry: Grayscale Mode - Toggle a grayscale screen filter from the menu bar or a shortcut. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/rkbhochalya/grayscale-mode) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Grayscale Mode - Manage grayscale mode from menu bar.

summary.one_liner: An open-source macOS menu bar app for toggling a grayscale screen filter, with a configurable global shortcut and per-app exclusions.
summary.what_it_does: Grayscale Mode is a macOS menu bar app that lets you switch the screen to grayscale from the status bar. The README says it works on any screen and offers a configurable shortcut, defaulting to ⌥⌘G. It also has an option to disable grayscale for selected apps. The README lists three dependencies: LaunchAtLogin for launch-at-login support, Defaults for UserDefaults handling, and MASShortcut for global keyboard shortcuts. The README does not describe installation steps beyond a download link, and it has no screenshots in the text.
use_cases: Toggle grayscale screen to reduce distraction
Switch screen to black and white quickly from the menu bar
Set a keyboard shortcut for grayscale on macOS
Keep grayscale off for specific apps such as design tools
Launch a grayscale toggle automatically at login
how_to_run: Download the latest version from the repository's Download section
notable: Per-app option to disable grayscale for selected apps
Lives in the macOS menu bar on any screen
Launch at login support via LaunchAtLogin
caveats: The README gives no build or install instructions beyond a download link
Copyright notice covers images and assets, which are excluded from the MIT license
